newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts officials urge Keno cap before lottery probe.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts officials urge Keno cap before lottery probe.

text.p: As Massachusetts legislators begin hearing testimony Wednesday into abuses in the Massachusetts lottery program uncovered by the Boston Globe, lottery officials urged stopping the expansion of Keno.

Treasurer Joe Malone, a Republican is expected to ask lawmakers to ban new licenses for the $400 million-a-year video numbers game. Malone's proposal will cap the number of Keno licenses at its present level of 1,585 - well short of the 3,000 licenses the 1993 legislation anticipated.

The Globe published a series of articles in February detailing abuses associated with lottery expansion, including widespread addiction, missuse of coupons, sales to minors and targeting poor neighborhoods.

Lottery Director Sam DePhillippo said in a press release that legislative action will be needed to impose the cap. The Massachusetts lottery, which has the highest per capita sales in the nation, is a $3 billion-a-year business.
Convenience stores around the state are likely to oppose any Keno cap and the Democratically controlled Legislature may hestiate as well because the revenues provide local aid for cities and towns.
Meanwhile, the state's Attorney General Scott Harshbarger, a Democrat, held a press conference on Tuesday urging legislators to reject efforts to legalize casino gambling in Massachusetts.
Republican Gov. William Weld, who has been hedging on whether to seek a third-term, reiterated his support for the Wampanoag Indian Tribe casino to be built in southeastern Massachusetts.
Harshbarger and Malone are both expected to run for the governor's seat next year.
